Putt's first submission in over a month.

Also, Putt commented in a bug thread as himself, and also as two of his alts.

This is pretty exciting. Active use of his account answers some questions, but certainly not all.

My analysis of this situation: bug appears/reappears/is discovered, very easily exploitable and has potential to render large portions of this website unusable. PuttItOut, having historically been closely tied to most bug-fixing issues, emerges from the shadows and contributes a funny submission and some comments.

My interpretation: all of this content he posted is humourous/playful and I would argue also in his usual character. It was also rather brief, which though provides little to analyze, is also in original character.

My hypothesis: Putt never wanted to be centre stage, in the limelight, exposed to the world, or out there in anyway. When he first climbed into the Voat playpen he was potentially/likely most interested in contributing in terms of hard code, and not so much PR. One of the first comments of his I ever read after joining Voat was simply: "I like being the underdog". Back then he was never centre stage, never in the limelight. He did the work he liked, behind the scenes, and very occasionally would do an announcement (and that's a heavy "very"). More recently, Putt has been doing virtually all of the announcements, for quite some time. He was also predominantly behind subverse transfers and most visibly involved in bug fixes. A lot seemed to fall on Putt in recent weeks and months.

I don't know the exact details concerning what Putt and Atko have been doing these last few months, but I'm certain there has been plenty to do. Neither Putt nor Atko have the time to work full-time or even really part-time on Voat. Working on Voat does not pay. They have other jobs for that. I feel it is possible, and frankly likely, that Atko, and perhaps more recently Putt, have stepped back from Voat in order to limit the stress in their lives. Putt has withdrawn back into the shadows, staying silent as long as he can and doing what work he can find time to do, leaving Atko back in the centre stage.

If this is truly all that has gone on with Putt recently, then the inevitable consequence is what we have recently been able to observe--more Atko. Admin communication has been I would say at an all-time low, at least since I joined in July of 2015, and what little of the admins we've seen has primarily been posts by Atko, even while Atko was allegedly on vacation. This is fine, except that it's been clear for a while that Voat has become a heavy load to bear (we're pretty big, goats, especially for a website run by two people), and even with Putt supposedly working behind the scenes, that leaves Atko with much of the PR work. Coupled with a full-time job and whatever programming work Atko is left with, we're left with a couple of busy and stressed out admins. I hope that this might explain any apparent silence or missing answers/explanations we have recently experienced, as well as Atko's response to the strikethrough bug.

Atko and Putt have lots to do, no time to do it (they've stated this multiple times before), and in the comment thread to which I just linked, Atko admits that Voat is clearly understaffed. Two people is not enough for a website this big. Plain and simple.

Conclusion: I think the Putt that has recently appeared is indeed the One True Putt. I may be wrong; it's not easy to tell things like this. But I see no reason to think he is other than himself. I think Atko is Atko too. I don't think they've been replaced. Whether they've been gagged is still unclear, but concerns raised about Atko as yet not explicitly saying that there have been no requests of any kind...I don't know if this is truly a concern, simply because of the unreliability of warrant canaries in the first place. We've been told that there have been no NS/FISA requests, but some users want to have more broad denials, but I think any denials of this kind have to be taken with grains of salt anyway.

That's all for now. Voat is not broken or dying, though it could most definitely use some help, and our Putt seems to still be out there, lurking in the shadows and continuing to do what he can for this wonderful website with what little time he has.

Thank you @Atko and @PuttItOut. Putt, I hope you agree to do the AMA with Atko. I would love for that to happen.
